title: SmaRTLy: RTL Optimization with Logic Inferencing and Structural Rebuilding
problem: Traditional RTL multiplexer optimization in tools like Yosys only monitors control port values during tree traversal, missing intrinsic logical relationships among signals and opportunities for structural optimization.
motivation: Multiplexer trees are ubiquitous in RTL designs; better optimization of these structures can significantly reduce gate count and improve design efficiency.
method: The approach uses logic inferencing—analyzing how signals logically depend on each other—to identify redundant multiplexers, which are circuit structures that select inputs based on control signals. It eliminates these unnecessary multiplexers entirely. For the remaining multiplexers, it restructures them by leveraging the discovered signal dependencies, reducing the total number of logic gates in the design.
key_novelty: The core innovation is analyzing signal dependencies to both identify and restructure redundant multiplexers, rather than only tracking control values.
contributions: Logic inferencing method to identify redundant multiplexer trees
Structural rebuilding technique for remaining multiplexers based on signal dependencies
8.95% additional AIG area reduction vs. Yosys on IWLS-2005 and RISC-V benchmarks
47.2% more AIG area removal than Yosys on industrial designs (>1M gates)

metrics.area: 8.95% reduction vs. Yosys on IWLS/RISC-V; 47.2% more reduction on industrial benchmarks

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation focuses on open benchmarks and single industrial design.
primary_theme: RTL multiplexer optimization via logic inferencing and structural rebuilding
